Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 502s (ClearSky)

I've pulled runtime traces and policy diffs. Quick summary: we rolled a global rate-window refinement at 08:30 PT to tighten burst windows on a handful of high-usage tenants flagged in the last policy sweep. ClearSky matched a recently added tag ("high-burst-risk") and got the conservative burst cap applied automatically.

Symptoms match: the burst window reduction causes sustained requests from ClearSky's bursty exporter to queue and then get rejected once KV cache pressure exceeded threshold; that shows up as 429s cascading to 502s for upstream retries.

Mitigation steps I've initiated:
1) Reverted the burst-window change for the ClearSky tenant (pushed at 09:33 PT).
2) Increased short-term token concurrency for their pool to drain existing queues.
3) Created a hotfix to whitelist production traffic patterns for known integrations during staged policy rollouts.

I'll keep logs attached. Expect a measurable drop in 429s within the next 5–10 minutes. If not, we'll open a kernel-level throttle bypass.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 502s (ClearSky)

Looping in ops leadership. Brief findings so execs have visibility:
- Root cause: policy-rollout logic applied a conservative burst-window override based on an automated rule that used a noisy heuristic (7d peak average + tag inference). That heuristic misclassified ClearSky due to a short promo traffic spike last week.
- Why it mattered: the updated burst-window was overly restrictive for ClearSky's usual traffic distribution (short high-QPS bursts). Our serving runtime queued and then back-pressured upstream causing retries and 502s.

Immediate actions taken: revert for tenant, raised short-term capacity, and blocked the heuristic from being applied to any tenant with an active enterprise contract until we add a manual review gate.

Next steps (24–72h):
- Postmortem with signal-level analysis and corrected heuristic (Connor/Marcus)
- Customer incident brief + credit proposal (Avery + Laura)
- Backfill automation test that simulates burst profiles against policy changes (SRE/runtime test harness)

I'll prepare an exec note for Legal/Finance if we need to move on credits, but CS should coordinate messaging.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-09-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: ClearSky incident update and next steps

Samir / Emily — final update and actions. Apologies again for the disruption. Summary of what happened and what we'll do next:

What happened:
- A policy roll-out at 08:30 PT applied a conservative burst-window override to ClearSky due to an automated classification heuristic. That override reduced the tenant's allowed instantaneous burst capacity and created queueing/429s that cascaded to 502s.

What we did:
- Reverted the rule at 09:33 PT; increased short-term concurrency to drain queues; implemented a temporary whitelist for enterprise tenants during policy rollouts.
- We are preparing a postmortem with signal-level charts (will share 24 hours).

Planned remediation and customer assurances:
- Fix the heuristic and add a manual review step for enterprise-tagged tenants before policy changes.
- Add canary gates that simulate tenant burst profiles before wide rollout.
- Offer a one-time usage credit for the impacted window (proposal attached in the incident brief).

Attachments: s1 incident brief (slo-incident-brief_CSH-20270908.pdf) and the traffic snapshot you provided.

If you want a quick call to walk through details, I'm available today 16:00–17:30 PT. We value ClearSky's partnership and will treat this with priority.

Regards,
Avery Johnson
Account Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
